newsitem.title: UK: Marley prospects encouraging, 97 starts well.
newsitem.headline: Marley prospects encouraging, 97 starts well.

text.p: Marley Plc, the UK building materials group, said on Wednesday that despite poor weather conditions across Europe in early January, 1997 had started well and that prospects were encouraging.

Marley announced the outlook with its annual results which showed pretax profit up to 85 million stg versus 46.3 million stg. Turnover rose to 677.4 million from 637.8 million and the dividend was up to five pence from 4.7 pence per share.
The profit figure was inflated by exceptional items, with a 41.7 stg gain from disposals in 1996. Operating profits from continuing operations rose 12 percent.

On 1997, Marley said: "Prospects for the majority of our overseas markets are encouraging and the improving trend in new housebuilding in the UK, which started in the latter stages of 1996, appears to be continuing."
The group added that it was well positioned and it still aimed to expand its plastics operations.
Looking at a divisional breakdown of the results, plastic products' turnover was up to 428.7 million, from 381.3 million, with profits at 38 million versus 29.4 million.
Concrete and clay sales fell to 251.6 million from 256.5 million, with profits down to 13.1 million from 15.8 million.
